- Priority: embeddings + reranking pipeline first, then structured tool-calls for case enrichment.
- Constraints: must validate auth options (API-key for PoC, OIDC for prod), and confirm network isolation options for compliance.

2) Karthik will share a short auth playbook explaining API keys, scoped tokens, and OIDC integration. Attachment: auth-playbook.md
3) Marissa will provision a temporary demo tenant with traffic-limited quotas so you can run reranker experiments. I’ll post the HubSpot deal and share access. Link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/DP-4732

Quick dev notes (more details to follow from Karthik):
- SDKs: we recommend Redwood SDK v0.14.x for Python and @redwood/sdk v0.9.x for TypeScript for compatibility with our routing APIs.
- Local testing: the sample apps include a local proxy (docker-compose) that simulates prefix caching and KV behavior so experiments are representative.

Thanks — I’ll send the attachments and Karthik will follow up with the auth steps.

Chloe — adding technical specifics for the sample apps so BrightPath can boot the environment quickly. Quoting your note below for context.

On Sat, 24 Apr 2027 at 14:05, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Alex / BrightPath eng team — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can get your engineers running locally with representative payloads.
> 
> [snip]

Engineer checklist (run in order):
1) Local prerequisites
   - Docker 24.x, docker-compose, Node 18+, Python 3.10+.
   - Install redis for local KV cache (sample uses redis://localhost:6379) but docker-compose will create a container if you prefer.
2) Auth options (PoC -> Prod)
   - PoC: scoped API key (short TTL, per-tenant) — easiest to get started.
   - Prod: OIDC + token exchange (we provide token introspection endpoint and roles mapping). See auth-playbook.md.
3) Routing & model selection
   - Use routing rules to send short queries (<200 tokens) to the low-cost embedding + reranker path; long-form tool-calls routed to a structured-output-capable model.
   - Example policy: route by route_id in request header: "x-rd-route: rerank-v1" or "x-rd-route: toolcall-v1".
4) Embeddings & reranker pattern
   - Precompute paragraph embeddings (batching allowed) and store in your vector DB.
   - For reranking: fetch top-N candidates, call Redwood rerank endpoint with candidates array and prompt template.
5) Structured output / tool calling
   - Use the SDK's tool_call schema to declare tool bindings; sample shows a small enrichment tool that accepts JSON input and returns structured case fields.

Quick start commands (Python)
- create virtualenv, install: pip install redwood-sdk==0.14.2
- run sample: python samples/bridge_demo/run_local.py --api-key REDWOOD_POC_KEY --route rerank-v1

Quick start (TypeScript)
- npm ci && npm run start:local (uses .env for REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_ROUTE)
- Example request (curl):
  curl -X POST
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDWOOD_POC_KEY'
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
    -d '{"route_id":"rerank-v1","input":"search query","candidates":["doc1","doc2"]}'
    http://localhost:8080/v1/rerank

Notes on observability for the spike:
- Enable token-level logging in the sample (flag: --verbose-tokens) to validate unit costs.
- Use the included Postman collection (sample-requests.postman_collection.json) to replay testcases.

I’ll drop the auth-playbook and a small README into the Drive folder. If they plan to test within a corporate network that requires egress restrictions, we can provide a Private deployment checklist.

—Karthik
